gen-gf-unica-one-gf-momo-trust-display: Momo Trust Display drifts along with loosely spaced letters and a generous x-height, clean and unhurried. And Unica One is the one that hits hardest, its strokes drawn at a single thickness, while the body font simply lets the lines breathe.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-mukta: Blunt, bold, and oddly open. Mukta follows in a plain sans with tall-bodied small letters, and if Unica One were shrunk down, its commanding presence would thin out fast.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-mukta-mahee: Unica One's huge lowercase eye gives it a look you won't confuse with anything else. Mukta Mahee brings chunky, tall lowercase letters that feel friendly, and that sturdy warmth is what holds the pair together.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-mukta-malar: Mukta Malar keeps its ascenders compressed, so a plain sans line sits low and tidy. But the strongest quality here is Unica One's marker-tip strokes, which give the whole pair a distinctive, commanding edge.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-mukta-vaani: Contemporary, with a commanding streak. Mukta Vaani has a high-waisted lowercase, and if Unica One were made small, its daylight-filled curves would lose the punch that gives them presence.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-narnoor: Unica One shows off a very large lowercase eye and curves with visible daylight inside them. Narnoor, a plain sans with short ascenders above big bowls, does the quiet work, while the heading handles the commanding part.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-play: Unica One draws curves as heavy as its stems, almost like cord, and that is what makes it stand out. And Play, a sans-serif with a faint upstroke-downstroke shift, deserves a size generous enough to show it.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-port-lligat-sans: Port Lligat Sans packs its characters in tight, with bowls left open on one side and barely any step down from capitals. And Unica One, with its marker-like constant line, supplies the commanding presence the body keeps in check.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-ramabhadra: Unica One draws every line like a plotter pen, one weight throughout, with a very large lowercase eye. Ramabhadra handles the reading, its prominent x-height keeping a sans-serif text easy to follow.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-rambla: Loud on top, level underneath. Unica One is the one with commanding presence and constant-width lines, while Rambla's small letters rising nearly to capital height do the steadier job of carrying the sans-serif text.
